A.api_summary:
Everything below is in cbba_sota.dyn.env unless noted.

Building an env
- make_env(source: TaskEnv | Instance | path, real: Realization | None = None, *, coalition="auto"|"arrival"|"decision", obs="causal"|"oracle", lease_L=200.0, abandon_on_failure=True) -> DynTaskEnvX
  - DynTaskEnvX is a class swap onto a copy of the TaskEnv (third_party is not edited).
  - The default realization is perturb.static_realization, i.e. the static env.
  - coalition="auto" means arrival order in run_plan and decision order in policy and native loops.

Running an episode
- DynTaskEnvX.run_plan(controller: Controller | None = None, routes: list[list[int]] | None = None, *, max_time=200.0, skip_finished=True) -> Episode
  - Plan following in the env's own loop. Routes use 0-based task ids.
- DynTaskEnvX.run_policy(policy: Policy, *, shuffle_seed: int | None = None, max_time=200.0, observer=None) -> Episode
  - Mirrors rl._episode (Worker.run_episode).
- The native loops also work on the subclass: rl.rollout, greedy._run_nearest, execute_by_route. Failure onsets and detections are processed inside next_decision, so a native driver gets D6 too. Agent D's run_b1 drives run_policy and gives episodes identical to my RLPolicy.

Controller and policy protocols
- Controller.on_events(env, t, events: list[Event]) -> bool | None
  - Called once per epoch that has events. Return True if it re-planned.
  - Event(kind, t, tasks, agents, info) with .structural and .get(key).
  - Structural kinds: release, failure, abandon, idle, membership.
  - Noise kinds: finish, wasted, window_end, wakeup.
- Policy.selectable(env, i) -> bool and Policy.act(env, i) -> int (1-based task id, 0 = depot).
- Provided policies:
  - RLPolicy(net, *, sample=False, seed=0, device="cpu"). It deletes known-failed agent rows via drop_failed_rows(env, agent_id, task_obs, agent_obs, mask).
  - NearestPolicy(max_waiting=True): the paper greedy.

Actions and views for controllers
- set_route(i, tasks) -> bool (released tasks only, 0-based) and route(i) -> list[int]
- abandon(i) -> bool
- request_wakeup(t)
- post_event(Event)
- drain_events() -> list[Event]
- state() -> StateView, the causal snapshot. Fields: t, H, released, finished, started, start, committed, present, residual[T,K], alive, mode (home|to_home|travel|wait|work|idle|failed), target, pos, dep, tau, stall, eta, routes, dur_nom.
- nominal_instance() -> Instance (nominal durations; Instance.from_env would read the realized ones).
- predict_ready(view, kappa=1.0) -> (ready[A], at[A], task_finish[T]), the Section 4.1 predictor.
- position(i, t=None) -> xy, stall-aware and frozen at failure.
- known_failed() and is_failed(i), the contract agent D's driver uses; realization property; may_go_home().
- legs[i]: list of (decided, departure, nominal_tau, target_id) per agent.
- signature() and world (a string with the rule in force and the env code hash; code_hash() gives the hash alone).

Episode fields
- world, makespan (None if the episode never ended), success, completion, env_finished
- travel, wait, wasted_trips, abandons, restarts, failures, detected, decisions
- controller_calls, replans, route_versions, structural_events, epochs
- cpu_event_s: per controller call with a structural event, or per policy decision
- cpu_total_s
- property makespan_or_cap

issues_and_caveats: D2 versus RL: the spec's regression '15 RL rollouts identical under arrival order' holds only for plans made from RL rollouts, not for the live RL policy on MA-AT. Its coalitions are non-minimal, so a redundant late member leaves early and the whole rollout changes, often to RL's benefit (3 of 4 samples in my smoke test). Default coalition='auto' uses decision order for policies (the native, bit-identical choice) and arrival order for plan following (identical under good comms with minimal covers). Arrival-order RL is available as a sensitivity via --coalition arrival; recommend reporting it for B1 fairness (K3).

Native greedy quirk: in natively failing greedy episodes (e.g. MA-AT-25-5-50 dev 1, makespan 200.46), the native env's lease removes a waiting member at t >= 200, and native back-dating then departs it at time 0 (the uncovered task's time_finish). D4 back-dates only agents that worked on their previous task, so only such post-cap legs differ.

Failed robots' agent rows are deleted, not zeroed. Agent D found that a zero row 0 makes the released network return NaN. RLPolicy and D's B1Policy delete rows identically and gave identical episodes on F1-R2, F3-pf0.2 and F3-pf0.2-R2.

Two D4 generalizations: the cap uses the latest release or failure-detection epoch, and when H > 0 trips home are never back-dated. The second was found by a failing test: RL agents were back-dated home before the last task finished. Both are no-ops when static.

B1 policy deadlock under F3: 5 of 480 RL episodes (MA-AT-25-5-50 dev 12 and 19, seed 1) end with every live robot waiting at a different uncovered task. With the good-comms 'detector' lease nobody gives up, so no epoch remains and the episode fails. This is a policy outcome, not an env defect. The lease_L option exists; the spec's shared lease grid should be tuned for B1 on dev (agent D).

Failure detection is global (good comms: onset + 5 ticks), and the env does the physical cleanup at detection: coalition removal, and reset of an aborted task, which restarts from scratch. For C3 (agent C) a comm-dependent detection would need an option to decouple knowledge from this cleanup; not implemented.

Not implemented: a rally/goto-waypoint action (needed by C3; legs are atomic as in the native env, with no mid-leg redirection), the Start-Kit Poisson event model and Gaussian delay lengths, and noise events other than finish and wasted (no start/arrival/stall events).
Delay calendars match the Start-Kit semantics in distribution (tested against a transcription of nextTick), but use numpy PCG64 per robot rather than the Start-Kit's shared mt19937 stream.
The failure exclusion rule is conservative and method-independent: the robots that never fail must cover every task. No dev F3 realization in the campaign was excluded (0 of 240).

D7 as specified ('home only when t >= H and every known task is finished') keeps idle robots in the field until the last finish, which lengthens makespans compared with the native 'all covered' rule when H > 0. It applies equally to all methods, in any driver, because agent_step enforces it.

The idle event fires only on the transition to idle. With H = 0 (F0, F3 without release) robots with an empty route go home natively, so no idle events occur there; the failure event is the re-plan trigger.
OL-construct (open-loop constructor, descriptive smoke only) fails under F3 by design, since it has no repair.

Package cbba_sota.dyn. Pinned kernel commit 4cf5e04; `__init__.py` files not edited.

Belief and planner (cbba_sota.dyn.planner):
- `PlanState(inst, now, released[T], done[T], started[T], committed[T], members: list[tuple], keys[T], alive[A], ready[A], pos[A,2], pos_task[A] (task id | AT_DEPOT=-2 | AT_POINT=-1), head[A] (committed task the robot travels to or waits at, -1 none), kappa=1.0, est=None, key_floor=-1.0)`
  - `PlanState.static(inst)`: time 0, all tasks released, robots at depots.
  - `.open_tasks()`.
- `SearchConfig(...)`: pinned v2 ALNS defaults, plus `floor="regret"|"insert"` and `keys="monotone"|"relaxed"` (default monotone = spec 4.1).
- `RHPlanner(cfg).plan(state, incumbent=None, scope=None, seed=0, iters=300, removable=None|bool[T]|callable(prob, sol, warm)->bool[Tk], warm=True, restarts=0, restart_noise=0.2, return_problem=False) -> DynPlan`
  - `iters=0` is insertion-only.
- `RHPlanner.evaluate(state, plan)` and `RHPlanner.extract(prob, sol, like, cpu)`.
- `DynPlan`: `members[T]`, `keys[T]` (nan = not planned), `makespan` (predicted), `unplaced`, `residual`, `demoted`, `released`, `iterations`, `seed`, `cpu_s`, `floor_makespan`, `n_open`, `n_anchored`, `routes_for(n_agents)`.
- `check_plan(state, plan, scope=None, relaxed=False) -> list[str]`: the plan contract (minimal covers, frozen members, key monotonicity or committed order, head-first, failed robots unrouted).
- Also: `state_digest(state) -> bytes`, `Problem(state, scope, relaxed)` (kernel instance), `travel_from`.

Kernels (cbba_sota.dyn.rh_kernels): state-start ALNS (ready/dout/dhome, est, fixed members, modes 0 free / 1 anchored / 2 residual, removable mask, head locks, unplaced penalty). Reduces bit for bit to 4cf5e04.

SPARC (cbba_sota.dyn.sparc):
- `RollingPolicy(triggers=STRUCTURAL, seed_base=0)`:
  - `.triggered(kinds)`;
  - `.replan(state, scope=None, event_index=None) -> DynPlan` is the comm-layer hook: seed = derive_seed(state_digest(state), event_index, seed_base); updates `.incumbent`;
  - `.on_event(executor, t, kinds)`, `.decisions` log.
- `SPARCConfig(iters=300, iters0=None, triggers=STRUCTURAL, seed_base=0, search=SearchConfig(), warm=True)`; `SPARC(config, name=None)`.
- `insertion_only()`, `every_event_rh(iters=300)` (structural + finish), `OpenLoop(iters0)`, `derive_seed(digest, event_index, seed_base)`.
- STRUCTURAL = {release, orphan, idle, membership}; NOISE_KINDS = {finish, start, arrive, stall}.

G4 fallback is my design. A residual that cannot be covered at its rank is first moved behind the committed prefix (demoted). Under good comms the env abandons present survivors at failure detection (lease = failure detector), so residual repair mostly applies to en-route members.

issues_and_caveats: Decision needed before the C3 map (day 4-5), affecting K5/K6. Spec 4.5 says outsiders of the station component keep their believed routes and their traits count. Fed literally to agent B's key-monotone kernel (frozen_model='anchor', the default), an outsider's whole future route becomes residual anchors, which G1 places ahead of every repaired task; in-scope robots added to them then idle until the outsider arrives. On one toy-world instance: CEN-F at rho=1 gives 166.7 with anchoring vs 96.9 with frozen_model='head' (FULL 45.5), and SPARC at rho=1 gives 153.5 vs 85.7. This touches every arm with station anchoring (CEN-F, HYB, SPARC, DS). A faithful fix needs B's kernel to support pinned members with ready times outside the committed prefix; the pilots' list scheduler interleaved such tasks by start time. Single instance, surrogate physics: a signal, not an effect size.

Membership-triggered re-plans are costly under partial knowledge. Toy world, rho=2: 64.2 with membership triggers vs 51.6 without. Under ideal comms, 3x more re-plans cost only 45.5 -> 47.7. I added membership_debounce=0.5, matching the pilots' rate limit; it is a new tunable parameter not in spec 4.7 and should be frozen or declared.
Trigger defaults are my reading of Section 5.3: structural (V2) for CEN-F, REP-clamp, INF-r and SPARC; V1 for HYB's stranded components. They are ArmSpec fields and should be frozen with the spec.

Convention choices to freeze with the spec: per-node budget of 1500 B per tick; ByteModel sizes; the digest is the whole version vector (361 B per frame at 50/50), which dominates total bytes, so C3 byte metrics should report delta_bytes separately; beacon budget 222 B (LoRa SF7 maximum payload); member_window 1.5; T2 heartbeat period 1.0 vs one tick with ideal comms; Rayleigh sensitivity calibrated to a mean in-disk drop of p at a declared 1000 m per unit.
Link-up is checked at both ends of each tick. This is exact for straight legs (convexity) and approximate when a robot turns inside a tick (at most 0.02 distance).
GE advances per tick per directed link (CV_MRTA advances per message). They coincide because every node broadcasts once per tick, and it keeps CRN.
New contacts cost one extra digest-handshake tick (anti-entropy design); cbja relays such a message one tick faster.

Compute for the C3 map: at rho=0.5, stranded leaders re-planned up to 2250 times per episode in the toy world (HYB, MA-AT-25), and one episode took 46 s of wall time at 300 iterations on the loaded host. The full grid (arms x rho x families x 80 instances x 2 seeds) needs a budget plan within the 8-process cap.

  (2) Coalitions were frozen lazily at the next call, re-adding robots that had left since; they are now frozen from env.legs at the departure.
  (3) The lease = failure-detector rule now also covers frozen partners that had not departed.
  (4) A commitment ends when its task starts, also when the task was started and reset between two calls.

B4 implementation overhead: `RHPlanner.plan` rebuilds the kernel `Problem` for every restart (about 70% of B4's per-restart CPU). B4-eq was charged for constructions only, which is generous to B4.
